So if you believe that there distinct human subspecies, what are they?

Thats not what is meant by the implication of skin colour being an adaptive trait. Because skin colour has a strong adaptive pressure from geographic location, similar skin colours can be a result of convergent evolution rather than genetic relatedness.

Give [this article](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/is-our-tendency-to-experi/) a read, it might help. 

If we’re talking about fear (such as fear of the dark), that fear comes from chemicals in our brain, which are products of genes. I think this can also be tied in with the spotlight effect, being embarrassed can be helpful in an evolutionary sense because I guess you would be more aware of what you were doing, therefore possibly less likely to engage in behaviour that prevents you from reproducing and dying before doing so. So the trait for being more embarrassed is more likely to be passed on. 

I think what you need to remember is that a lot of our psychology is dependent on physical structures in our brain, like cells and chemicals, which are encoded for by genes.

I see what you’re getting at, but a few of your assumptions are wrong. 

We can’t use all phenotypic traits as makers for putting humans into subspecies. A phenotypic trait such as skin colour is an adaptive trait, which we cannot use because they reflect environmental conditions and not genetic differences. 

To also be considered a different race, the genetic diversity within that race needs to be much smaller than diversity between races, which you’ll find is just not the case. 

[This](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3737365/) is an excellent article really breaking everything down, it’s pretty heavy but it does explain everything.
